neighbours.label: number or quantifier counting the parts in an anatomical description ('with four pairs of legs', 'fibers connect different structures')
fire: Ticks are arachnids, small animals with four pairs of legs and no antennae.
Insects are arthropods with three pairs of legs and a body in three parts.
Crabs are decapods, crustaceans with five pairs of legs including the claws.
Association fibers link different regions within one hemisphere of the brain.
Short arcuate fibers connect different gyri lying next to each other in the cortex.
Harvestmen are arachnids with four pairs of very long, thin legs.
Commissural fibers join different areas of the left and right hemispheres.
Mites, like spiders, are arachnids with four pairs of jointed legs.
quiet: Ticks are arachnids that feed on the blood of mammals and birds.
Insects are arthropods that change from larva to adult during metamorphosis.
Crabs are decapods that live in oceans, rivers and even on land.
Damage to the white matter can slow thinking and movement in older adults.
The surface of the cortex is folded into ridges and grooves.
Harvestmen are often seen on walls and fences in late summer.
Brain scans can show where blood flow rises during a task.
Mites, like spiders, are often found in household dust.
